content.text: : USU ascending infect of lower urinary tract from urethra
•lower tract = cystitis · upper tract = pyelo - pyelo common cause of UTI in <1y
: female (10-fold risk over males) - urinary tract abnormality → stasis · obstruct or reflux
•sexual activity · neurogenic bladder · VUR · indwelling catheter · recent instrumentation · immunodeficiency · uncircumcised boys · <2y
· sepsis - ± strong · foul-smelling or cloudy urine
•<2y (can't verbalize urinary Sx): consider UTI w fever, esp fever w.o clear source - febrile <2y w ⍉other Sx → high suspicion
•>2y classic: dysuria · freq · urgency · new-onset incont · suprapubic pain · hematuria
•fever · chills · flank pain · CVA tenderness → suggest upper UTI (pyelo) - vomiting nonspecific, more likely upper
PE: CVA · abd or suprapubic tenderness · palpable bladder · voiding problems (dribbling · poor stream · straining)
· hematuria · WBCs esterase · nitrites · cloudy urine · bacteriuria
•supports dx - alone insuff · guides empiric tx while cx pending
: gold strd - ≥100,000 CFU/mL of single pathogen confirms
•toilet trained → midstream clean-catch · ⍉toilet trained → cath or suprapubic aspiration (criterion strd)
: vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) in 30-50% of peds w UTI <1yo
RBUS for anyone 2-24mo following first febrile UTI
: recurr · febrile UTIs · family hx of renal/urologic dz · poor growth or HTN · children who don't respond as expected to abx therapy
- empiric 2nd/3rd-gen cephalosporin (cefuroxime · cefdinir · cefixime) → per cx & susceptibility
- outpt if nontoxic: PO fluids + abx + close monitoring by caregiver
- Augmentin (⍉plain amoxicillin) · TMP-SMX - only if local resistance <15% · TMP-SMX if PCN & cephalosporin allergy (↑resistance) · also sexually active
- TMP-SMX in preg: may use in 2nd trimester · avoid 1st trimester (folic acid antagonist) & days before delivery (↑kernicterus)
- nitrofurantoin ⍉preferred (freq dosing) - use if cephalosporin w.in 2mo or sexually active (covers S. saprophyticus)
ADMIT: toxic · sepsis · dehydration (MC acute comp) · urinary obstruct · ⍉PO · <2mo w febrile UTI · <1mo w suspected UTI (even afebrile)
Afebrile · immunocompetent · ⍉GU hx → abx only if cx (+)
Infect of upper GU tract (kidney parenchyma & renal pelvis)
Organ- & life-threatening - comps: kidney scarring · kidney injury · HTN · dehydration (common)
: USU ascending infect of lower urinary tract - neonates: hematogenous spread
E. coli MC (bowel flora) - Klebsiella · Proteus · Enterococcus · rarely staph or GBS
: DM · hx of recurr UTIs or kidney stones · preg · congenital urinary tract malformations
Peds RF: VUR · delayed/incomplete voiding (neurogenic bladder) · constipation · catheterization · uncircumcised males
•neonates: fever · jaundice · poor feeding · vomiting · FTT
•school-age: fever · abd/flank pain · vomiting · diarrhea · ↓appetite · malodorous urine · hematuria
PE: toxic-appearing · in obvious discomfort - abd & suprapubic tenderness · palpable bladder - CVA tenderness more likely in older children
•children w fever >48h - collect w proper technique
•bladder cath = best in most infants & young children · clean-catch midstream if able to void · suprapubic aspiration if periurethral irritation or nonretractable foreskin
: definitive - obtain in all children w suspected pyelo
Upper vs lower UTI: BUN · Cr · ESR · CRP · procalcitonin · serum & urinary IL-6/IL-8
Renal U/S or nuclear cortical scan: struct abnorm & scarring - ⍉needed for dx
PO 2nd/3rd-gen cephalosporin (ex, cefixime) x10-14d or 2-4d IV → PO - 1st-gen if uncomplicated - cephalosporin preferred over FQs in children
(↑arthralgia · arthritis) - cipro approved for peds complicated UTI/pyelo but ⍉1st choice
•IV cefotaxime · ceftriaxone · cefepime or gentamicin x10-14d - ampicillin if enterococcus suspected (⍉empiric while cx pending) - definitive per cx & sensitivities
•gentamicin BBW: neurotoxicity · ototoxicity · nephrotoxicity · NM blockade
•IVF if ⍉tolerating PO - empiric abx + hydration + pain & fever control
•prompt dx & tx → prevents permanent kidney scarring
: older age · signs of obstruct · comorbid conditions · inability to tolerate PO abx · <2yo
